Based on the healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that amblyopia (lazy eye) can be a treatable condition. Here's a synthesized answer to your question:

Amblyopia is not always permanent and can be treated with appropriate care and treatment. The recovery of visual function in the amblyopic eye can occur over time after developing visual loss in one eye, similar to how some individuals recover from strabismus or other vision problems.

This process typically involves improving the strength and coordination between the healthy and affected eyes through various treatments, such as patching (using a special contact lens), glasses, or surgery. In some cases, the amblyopic eye may even regain 20/20 vision in the years following treatment, although this can vary depending on individual factors.

However, it's essential to note that not everyone with amblyopia will experience full recovery of their vision. Factors such as age, eye health, and type of visual loss can influence the likelihood of recovery.

It's also important to seek medical attention if you're experiencing any symptoms or concerns related to your eyes, including changes in vision, blurred vision, or eye discomfort. A healthcare professional can assess your eyes and provide guidance on the best course of treatment for your specific situation.
